paper.title: The Pareto Frontier of model selection for general Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection for contextual bandits with nested finite policy classes (adaptive adversary in contexts and losses)
unmapped: model selection over M nested policy classes Pi_1 subset ... subset Pi_M; regret bound must hold simultaneously for every class m
learner knows the sizes |Pi_m| of all policy classes and the number of classes M
settings.definition_quote: There are $K$ arms and nested policy classes $(\Pi_m)_{m=1}^M$, where a policy $\pi\in\Pi_m, \pi:\cX\rightarrow[K]$ ... Reg(T,Pi) = max_{pi in Pi} E[sum_t ell_{t,A_t} - ell_{t,pi(x_t)}]. ... all upper bounds hold in the stronger notion where both the losses and the contexts are adaptive

settings.name_in_paper: S-switch problem with adaptive adversary (lower bound)
unmapped: switch times chosen adaptively based on the learner's actions; i.i.d. Bernoulli losses within each phase
learner is informed of the number of switches so far (phase counter as context)
settings.definition_quote: The adversary switches the reward distribution up to $S$ many times ... A switch from phase $s<S+1$ to $s+1$ occurs when the player has played $\Nmax$ times an arm in $[K-1]$ in phase $s$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandit model selection with two nested policy classes (lower bound)
unmapped: model selection between nested policy classes Pi_1 subset Pi_2
settings.definition_quote: There are $k+1$ environments $(\cE_i)_{i=0}^k$ with $\Pi_2=\{\pi_i|i\in[k]\cup\{0\}\}$ policies and $\Pi_1=\{\pi_0\}$. In all environments, we have $K=3$ ...

algorithms.name: (1/2,R,beta)-hedged Tsallis-INF over generic stable base algorithms

symbols.C_frak: free trade-off parameter > 0 chosen by the learner

conditions: holds uniformly over all m in [M]
tuning: Hedged-FTRL tuned with parameter C_frak over M instances of EXP4

source.label: thm:upper main
source.quote: For any $\C>0$, we can tune Hedged-FTRL over a selection of $M$ instances of EXP4 operating on policy classes $\Pi_1,\dots\Pi_M$, such that the following regret bound holds uniformly over all $m\in[M]$ \Reg(T,\Pi_m) = \tilde\cO(\max\{\C,\frac{\ln|\Pi_m|}{\C}\}\sqrt{MKT}).

results.notes: Regret defined as max over policies of expected difference; holds for adaptive contexts and losses. Õ hides polylog in T and K only.

symbols.C_m: complexity of base algorithm m: it is (1/2, sqrt(C_m T))-stable
symbols.M_cls: number of base algorithms / policy classes

conditions: base algorithms are (1/2, sqrt(C_m T))-stable: Reg_Imp(T,B_m) <= E[sqrt(rho_{T,m})] sqrt(C_m T)
holds simultaneously for all m in [M]

source.label: thm:upper general
source.quote: Given a collection of base algorithms $(\cB_m)_{m=1}^M$ which are $(1/2,\sqrt{\C_m T})$-stable ... then the regret of ($1/2,R,\beta)$-hedged Tsallis-Inf with $R_m = \sqrt{\C_mT}$, $\beta_m = \frac{1}{M}\max\{1,\frac{\C^2}{\C_m}\}$ satisfies ... \Reg(T,\cB_m) \leq 2\max\{\C,\frac{\C_m}{\C}\}\sqrt{MT} + \sqrt{2MT}.

results.notes: Generic corralling result; regret against the base algorithm's comparator class. With EXP4, C_m = O(K ln|Pi_m|) giving Theorem 1.

symbols.C_frak: constant in the assumed regret guarantee Reg_SW(T,1) = O(C_frak sqrt(KT))

conditions: any algorithm with regret guarantee Reg_SW(T,1) = O(C_frak sqrt(KT))
holds even when the agent is informed about the number of switches up to time t

source.label: thm:adaptive simple
source.quote: For any $K\geq 3$, sufficiently large $T$, and any algorithm with regret guarantee $\Reg_{SW}(T,1) = \cO(\C\sqrt{KT})$, there exists for any number of switches $S=\Omega(\C^2)$ a stochastic bandit problem such that $\Reg_{SW}(T,S) = \Omega(\min\{\frac{S}{\C}\sqrt{KT},T\})$. This bound holds even when the agent is informed about the number of switches up to time t.

results.notes: Switch points chosen adaptively by the adversary. Implies a contextual bandit lower bound Omega(min{ln|Pi_S|/(C ln K) sqrt(KT), T}).

symbols.C_frak: constant in assumed guarantee Reg(T,Pi_1) = O(C_frak sqrt(T))
symbols.N_2: size |Pi_2| of the larger policy class

conditions: proper algorithms (policy choice independent of current context)
algorithm satisfies Reg(T,Pi_1) = O(C_frak sqrt(T)) in every environment

source.label: thm:stochastic simple
source.quote: There exist policy classes $\Pi_1\subset\Pi_2$ with $|\Pi_2| =\Omega(\C^2)$, such that if the regret of a proper algorithm is upper bounded in any environment by $\Reg(T,\Pi_1) = \cO(\C\sqrt{T})$, then there exists an environment such that $\Reg(T,\Pi_2) = \Omega(\max\{\C,\frac{\ln|\Pi_2|}{\C}\}\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Proof gives Omega(min{ln(k) sqrt(T)/C, T}). Corollary 1 (no alpha in [1/2,1) solves the open problem for adaptive adversaries or proper algorithms in stochastic case) follows from Theorems 3 and 4.

conditions: any algorithm (proper or improper) satisfying Reg(T,Pi_1) = PolyLog * O(T^alpha) for some alpha in [1/2,1)

source.label: thm: improper
source.quote: No algorithm (proper or improper) can satisfy the requirements of open problem \eqref{eq:open} for all stochastic environments.

results.notes: Theorem is qualitative; linear regret rate taken from proof sketch (there exists an environment with regret linear in T).
